title: Learn
description: Core Data Processing learning flow for Cambridge 9618 Paper 2.

blocks.text: Data processing means taking input data, performing useful processing, and producing output.

blocks.title: Before writing pseudocode, ask:
items: What data is given or input?
Do I need an IF condition?
Do I need a counter, total, highest or lowest variable?

slides.title: Total of Five Numbers
slides.problem: Input five numbers and output their total.
slides.code:
DECLARE num, total, i : INTEGER

total <- 0

FOR i <- 1 TO 5
    INPUT num
    total <- total + num
NEXT i

OUTPUT total
slides.explanation: Input: five numbers. Process: add each number to total. Output: final total.

slides.title: Try It - IPO
slides.task: Write pseudocode to input six numbers and output their total.
slides.expectedAnswer:

markScheme.criterion: Use a loop for six values

blocks.text: Most data processing questions involve several values. A loop is used to process each value.

slides.title: Loops, Counters and Accumulators: Key terms

blocks.label: Counter
blocks.text: A variable that increases by 1 when something is counted.

blocks.label: Accumulator
blocks.text: A variable that builds a running total.

slides.title: Loops, Counters and Accumulators: Code pattern
Count Values Greater Than 50
slides.problem: Input ten numbers and count how many are greater than 50.
slides.code:
DECLARE num, count, i : INTEGER

count <- 0

FOR i <- 1 TO 10
    INPUT num

    IF num > 50 THEN
        count <- count + 1
    ENDIF
NEXT i

OUTPUT count
slides.explanation: The loop processes each number. The IF checks the condition. The counter tracks how many numbers match.

blocks.text: Arrays store many related values under one identifier. In data processing questions, arrays let you process many values using an index.

slides.title: Arrays for Data Processing: Code pattern

blocks.text:
DECLARE Number : ARRAY[1:100] OF INTEGER

FOR i <- 1 TO 100
    INPUT Number[i]
NEXT i
